blocks.text: The Unity packages are in early development and the scene schema has a first version. Constructors and game generation are planned and have no repositories yet. Every package page states what exists today.
Source code lives in the [IT-Kamianets GitHub organization](https://github.com/IT-Kamianets).

installation.title: Installation
installation.lead: Install through the Unity Package Manager from Git.

items: Unity 6000.6
Git installed, so Unity can fetch packages by URL
For room scanning with `3d-unity-spatial`: the Meta XR MR Utility Kit (`com.meta.xr.mrutilitykit`) in your project
In Unity, open `Window › Package Manager`.
Choose `+ › Add package from git URL`.
Paste the URL of a package from the table below.

blocks.text: Dependencies are declared in each `package.json` and resolved by the Package Manager. Start with `3d-unity-core`.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.lead: Three layers, and scenes kept in an engine-independent format.

items: **Core packages** (`3d-*`): shared engine functionality such as scenes, assets, interaction, XR, and spatial data.
**Constructors** (`3d-constructor-*`): a starting architecture for one type of game, built on the core packages.
**Game-specific packages** (`game-<name>-*`): the rules, content, and assets of one game.

blocks.text: `3d-scene-schema` is the source of truth for a scene. Unity is not its permanent owner.

blocks.code: Scene Schema → Unity Scene → Scene Changes → Scene Schema

blocks.text: `3d-unity-scene` converts between the two. `3d-unity-xr` handles how people interact through XR hardware, and `3d-unity-spatial` understands the physical room and turns it into scene data.
Each line joins a package to one that needs it, as declared in each `package.json`.

items: Keep core packages reusable and product-independent.
Keep constructors focused on reusable gameplay architecture.
Keep game-specific logic outside the framework.
Prefer shared scene and asset structures between engines.
Let constructors compose existing packages instead of duplicating them.
Make generated projects easy to understand, modify, and extend.

examples.title: Examples
examples.lead: Scenes and workflows the packages are built for.

blocks.text: `3d-scene-schema` ships example scene documents in the `examples/` folder of its [repository](https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-scene-schema). Each one validates against the v1 schema.

items: `room-scan.example.json`: a scanned room described as one scene
`corridor-scan.example.json`: a corridor scan sharing a coordinate frame with the room scan

sections.title: From a room scan to a scene

blocks.text: The main workflow today: scan a real room on a Meta Quest, convert it to scene data, and store it as JSON.

items: `3d-unity-xr` triggers a scan from a controller button and shows progress in a HUD.
`3d-unity-spatial` reads the physical room and produces scene data.
`3d-unity-scene` converts it to a scene document that follows `3d-scene-schema`.
